_meanings:
.²1 the ceremonial ‘mountain of sugar’ (a heap measuring eight Bhāras)
 given away by pious donors together with four smaller

 mountains called Viṣkambhaparvata. Three golden trees are planted on
 the mountain, while on the smaller mountains are placed idols of Cupid,
 Kubera and Brahmā as well as a golden image of the Surabhi cow. It was
 customary to give away similar mountains of butter, salt, paddy, cotton
 and sesamum seeds; {#dAnAntaHSrutaSarkarAcalamaTaH KenAmftAnDAH smaraH#} <ls>N. 21. 154</ls>.
.²2 a sugar-loaf (conical).
a gift of sugar moulded in the shape of a cow; see {#SarkarAcala#}.
<ab>N.</ab> of an observance on the 7th day in the bright half of Vaiśākha.
